title: Pythagorean Theorem
subtitle: Right Triangles, Distance & 3D
bounds: PROTOCOL §4b Pythagorean (grade 8). Sides 1-10; every square 100 or less and every sum or difference of two squares (box diagonal: three) 100 or less. Whole answers come only from 3-4-5 and 6-8-10 (box diagonals 1-2-2 -> 3, 2-4-4 -> 6, 2-3-6 -> 7, 1-4-8 -> 9, 4-4-7 -> 9); every other length is an unsimplified √n, n 2-99 and not a perfect square. Coordinates of size 10 or less. Wrong choices up to 999. A root is compared with a whole number only when they differ by 0.3 or more.

tiers.name: Find the Hypotenuse
tiers.description: Legs given: square, add, take the root.

tiers.name: Find a Leg
tiers.description: Hypotenuse and one leg given: subtract the squares.

tiers.name: Is It a Right Triangle?
tiers.description: Test a^2 + b^2 = c^2 and spot the hypotenuse.

tiers.name: Distance on the Plane
tiers.description: Make a right triangle from two points.

tiers.name: Stories & 3D
tiers.description: Ladders, ramps, walks and box diagonals.

ADDED_LEGS.student: Adding the legs is the walk around, not the shortcut. Use a^2 + b^2 = c^2.
ADDED_LEGS.teacher: Hypotenuse taken as a + b (the sum of the legs).

NO_ROOT.student: That is c^2, the square. Take the square root to get c.
NO_ROOT.teacher: Stops at a^2 + b^2 (or c^2 − a^2) and forgets the final square root.

ROOT_OF_LEG_SUM.student: Square each side first: a^2 + b^2. Not a + b.
ROOT_OF_LEG_SUM.teacher: Takes the root of the plain sum of the sides, skipping the squares.

DOUBLED_FOR_SQUARE.student: Squaring a side is a × a, not 2 × a.
DOUBLED_FOR_SQUARE.teacher: Squares by doubling: a^2 read as 2a.

ADDED_SQUARES.student: Finding a leg, you subtract: c^2 − a^2. The hypotenuse is the big one.
ADDED_SQUARES.teacher: Adds the squares when a leg is missing, treating the known leg as if the hypotenuse were unknown.

SUBTRACTED_SIDES.student: Subtract the squares, not the sides: c^2 − a^2.
SUBTRACTED_SIDES.teacher: Finds the leg as c − a (plain difference of the sides).

ROOT_OF_DIFF.student: Square the sides first, then subtract and take the root.
ROOT_OF_DIFF.teacher: Takes the root of c − a, skipping the squares.

ADD_SIDES.student: Test squares, not sides: a^2 + b^2 = c^2, not a + b = c.
ADD_SIDES.teacher: Checks the converse with a + b = c instead of a^2 + b^2 = c^2.

ORDER_AS_GIVEN.student: The hypotenuse is the longest side, whatever order they are listed in.
ORDER_AS_GIVEN.teacher: Treats the last-listed (or first-two-listed) sides as the legs without finding the longest.

CONSECUTIVE.student: Only special sets work. 3, 4, 5 does; 4, 5, 6 does not. Test a^2 + b^2.
CONSECUTIVE.teacher: Generalises 3-4-5 to any three consecutive numbers.

CLOSE_ENOUGH.student: Close is not equal. a^2 + b^2 must equal c^2 exactly.
CLOSE_ENOUGH.teacher: Accepts a^2 + b^2 within a point or two of c^2.

ANY_TRIANGLE.student: Sides can make a triangle with no right angle. Test the squares.
ANY_TRIANGLE.teacher: Believes any three lengths that form a triangle make a right triangle.

LEG_AS_LONGEST.student: A root can be the longest side. Compare the squares to see.
LEG_AS_LONGEST.teacher: Picks a leg as the hypotenuse because the radical looks smaller than a whole number.

TAXICAB.student: Distance is the straight line, not across then up. Use a^2 + b^2 = c^2.
TAXICAB.teacher: Adds the horizontal and vertical gaps (taxicab distance).

ONE_LEG.student: Distance needs both gaps, across and up, squared and added.
ONE_LEG.teacher: Uses only the horizontal gap as the distance.

NEG_DIFF.student: Across zero the gap adds up: from −2 to 3 is 5, not 1.
NEG_DIFF.teacher: Subtracts sizes of coordinates on opposite sides of zero instead of adding them.

ADDED_ALL.student: Square each edge, add the squares, then take the root.
ADDED_ALL.teacher: Box diagonal taken as a + b + c.

FACE_ONLY.student: A box diagonal uses all three edges, not just one face.
FACE_ONLY.teacher: Gives a face diagonal (two edges) for the space diagonal.
